_meta.description: MITRE ATT&CK (Enterprise) mapping and ServiceNow best-practice guidance for each check in scans/. Keyed by '<level>/<id>' matching the MCP server's check ids.
_meta.methodology: Each check is mapped to the ATT&CK tactic(s)/technique(s) that the underlying misconfiguration most directly enables or resembles, following the common practice of crosswalking security controls to ATT&CK (as CIS Controls and NIST mappings do). These are practitioner-level, best-effort mappings authored for this repo and should be reviewed by a security analyst before being presented as authoritative in a client deliverable.
_meta.attack_version: Enterprise ATT&CK (techniques current as of v15/v16)

level-1/cstaces-1a-admin-users.rationale: Unreviewed, excessive admin/security_admin/user_admin assignment is the precondition attackers exploit via valid-account abuse and role manipulation to gain and keep privileged access.
level-1/cstaces-1a-admin-users.best_practice: Apply least privilege: limit admin/security_admin/user_admin to a named, documented set of individuals; run quarterly access certification; move service accounts to scoped roles.

level-1/cstaces-1b-multiple-high.rationale: Stacking multiple high-privilege roles on one account increases blast radius if that single account is compromised.
level-1/cstaces-1b-multiple-high.best_practice: Assign the minimum single role needed per function; avoid combining admin with security_admin/user_admin on the same account.

level-1/cstaces-1c-deprovioned-60newer.rationale: Recently inactive accounts that retain elevated roles are prime targets for credential reuse before deprovisioning catches up.
level-1/cstaces-1c-deprovioned-60newer.best_practice: Automate role revocation as part of the deactivation workflow; don't wait for a separate cleanup pass.

level-1/cstaces-1c2-deprovsioned-60older.rationale: Elevated roles left on accounts inactive for more than 60 days represent long-lived, unmonitored persistence opportunities.
level-1/cstaces-1c2-deprovsioned-60older.best_practice: Treat this as a hard SLA breach; auto-revoke privileged roles from any account inactive beyond your deprovisioning window.

level-1/cstaces-3b-has-impersonator.rationale: Impersonation lets a compromised account operate as any other user, masking attacker activity under a victim's identity.
level-1/cstaces-3b-has-impersonator.best_practice: Restrict the impersonator role to a tiny, audited set of admins; log and alert on every impersonation session.

level-1/cstaces-3b2-nested-impersonator.rationale: Impersonation granted transitively through group/role inheritance is easy to miss in access reviews and creates the same risk as direct grants.
level-1/cstaces-3b2-nested-impersonator.best_practice: Review role inheritance chains, not just direct grants, when auditing impersonation rights.

level-1/cstaces-4a-secadmin.rationale: security_admin can modify ACLs and security controls directly, making it one of the highest-value roles to compromise or abuse.
level-1/cstaces-4a-secadmin.best_practice: Limit security_admin to platform security owners; require change-control review for any security_admin grant.

level-1/cstaces-5a-integration-admins.rationale: Integration/service accounts with admin rights and long-lived credentials are high-value, low-visibility targets — compromise gives silent, broad access without an interactive login to flag.
level-1/cstaces-5a-integration-admins.best_practice: Scope integration users to the specific tables/APIs they need via scoped roles, not admin; rotate their credentials regularly.

level-2/cstaces-12-local-account-login.rationale: Local DB logins bypass SSO/MFA enforcement, giving attackers a weaker authentication path that isn't governed by the identity provider.
level-2/cstaces-12-local-account-login.best_practice: Enforce SSO redirection (glide.authenticate.multisso.redirect_to_sso); limit local auth to documented break-glass accounts with MFA.

level-2/cstaces-13-role-mgt-v2.rationale: Without Role Management v2's granular, auditable role administration, over-broad or undocumented role grants are harder to detect and control.
level-2/cstaces-13-role-mgt-v2.best_practice: Install and adopt Role Management v2 to get structured, auditable role request/approval workflows instead of ad hoc role assignment.

level-2/cstaces-4a-secadmin.rationale: security_admin can modify ACLs and security controls directly, making it one of the highest-value roles to compromise or abuse.
level-2/cstaces-4a-secadmin.best_practice: Limit security_admin to platform security owners; require change-control review for any security_admin grant.

level-2/cstaces-4b-acl-modif.rationale: Recent, unreviewed ACL/role changes are the platform-security analog of policy/firewall tampering — a common step to widen access or disable controls before further action.
level-2/cstaces-4b-acl-modif.best_practice: Route all ACL and role changes through change management; alert on and review ACL/role modifications outside approved change windows.

level-2/cstaces-4c-self-role-grant.rationale: A user granting themselves admin is a direct privilege-escalation action, whether from a compromised account or an insider.
level-2/cstaces-4c-self-role-grant.best_practice: Require dual control/approval for any role grant, especially self-grants; alert in real time on self-assigned elevated roles.

level-2/cstaces-4e-encryption-configs.rationale: Changes to encryption configuration can silently downgrade protection for data at rest, consistent with adversary attempts to weaken encryption controls.
level-2/cstaces-4e-encryption-configs.best_practice: Restrict and log access to encryption context/config tables; alert on any modification and validate against your approved encryption standard.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

level-2/cstaces-5b-active-oauth.rationale: Active OAuth tokens/clients are durable, often long-lived credentials that let an attacker (or former integration) authenticate without a password or MFA prompt.
level-2/cstaces-5b-active-oauth.best_practice: Inventory and review all OAuth client/token grants quarterly; revoke unused tokens and set short, enforced expirations.

level-3/cstaces-2a-acl-overly-perm.rationale: Overly permissive ACLs mean a standard, already-valid account can reach data/functions it shouldn't, without needing to escalate further.
level-3/cstaces-2a-acl-overly-perm.best_practice: Apply least-privilege ACL design; require explicit role/condition checks instead of broad or missing restrictions.

level-3/cstaces-2b-acls-dangerous.rationale: ACLs with risky scripted conditions (e.g., logic that evaluates true unintentionally) can be exploited or misconfigured to bypass intended access restrictions entirely.
level-3/cstaces-2b-acls-dangerous.best_practice: Audit script-based ACL conditions for logic that could evaluate true unintentionally; prefer role/condition-based ACLs over custom scripts where possible.

level-3/cstaces-8-domsep-users.rationale: Users without a proper domain assignment in a domain-separated instance can see or act across domain boundaries they shouldn't, undermining tenant isolation.
level-3/cstaces-8-domsep-users.best_practice: Ensure every user has an explicit domain assignment; review domain separation inheritance rules so no user defaults to global/top-domain access unintentionally.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11a-prop-block-n.rationale: If access isn't blocked by default when no user criteria exist, any KB missing explicit criteria becomes open-by-default, exposing its content to unauthorized collection.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11a-prop-block-n.best_practice: Set glide.knowman.block_access_with_no_user_criteria=true so missing criteria fail closed, not open.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11b-prop-apply-a.rationale: Without article-level criteria enforcement, KB-level restrictions can be bypassed by reaching individual articles directly.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11b-prop-apply-a.best_practice: Enable glide.knowman.apply_article_read_criteria so article-level access always inherits/enforces user criteria.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11c-prop-search-.rationale: Search indexes that ignore role-based security can surface restricted article content to users who shouldn't see it, via search results instead of direct access.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11c-prop-search-.best_practice: Enable glide.knowman.search.apply_role_based_security so search results always respect the same restrictions as direct access.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11d-prop-show-un.rationale: Exposing unpublished/draft articles can leak pre-release, incomplete, or sensitive internal content to users who should only see published, reviewed material.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11d-prop-show-un.best_practice: Keep glide.knowman.show_unpublished disabled outside controlled authoring/review contexts.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11e-prop-draft-v.rationale: Broad draft-view permissions let more users than intended see in-review content before it's approved.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11e-prop-draft-v.best_practice: Restrict the draft/review view role to knowledge management staff only.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11f-kb-no-can-re.rationale: A KB with no explicit Can Read criteria defaults to open access for anyone who can reach it — the most common root cause of KB data exposure.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11f-kb-no-can-re.best_practice: Require every active KB to define at least one Can Read user criteria scoped to its intended audience.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11g-kb-no-cannot.rationale: Without an explicit deny list, edge cases (e.g., guest or external users) can fall through to default-allow behavior.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11g-kb-no-cannot.best_practice: Pair Can Read with an explicit Cannot Read criteria to deny known-risky populations (guest, external users) regardless of other grants.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11h-kb-no-can-co.rationale: An unrestricted Can Contribute setting lets any authenticated user author/edit KB content, which can be used both to exfiltrate via new articles and to plant misleading or malicious content.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11h-kb-no-can-co.best_practice: Scope Can Contribute criteria to authorized authors/contributors only; never leave it empty on an active KB.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11i-kb-uses-any-.rationale: The 'Any User'/'Any user' criteria effectively disables access control for the KB, equivalent to leaving the content open to collection by anyone in the instance.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11i-kb-uses-any-.best_practice: Replace 'Any User'/'Any user' criteria with scoped group- or role-based criteria matching the intended audience.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11j-kb-guest-not.rationale: If Guest isn't explicitly denied, unauthenticated external visitors may be able to read internal KB content directly.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11j-kb-guest-not.best_practice: Add an explicit Cannot Read criteria for the Guest user on every active knowledge base unless public access is a deliberate, reviewed decision.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11k-kb-contrib-n.rationale: Granting contribution rights without a matching read restriction means contributors can add or alter content in a KB whose read boundary is undefined or broader than intended.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11k-kb-contrib-n.best_practice: Always pair Can Contribute criteria with a matching, equally-scoped Can Read criteria.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11l-kb-pre-2022-.rationale: Legacy KBs created before the platform's automatic guest-denial default don't inherit that protection and must be remediated individually.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11l-kb-pre-2022-.best_practice: Audit and explicitly add Guest denial criteria to every pre-2022 knowledge base; don't assume newer defaults apply retroactively.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11m-br-guest-use.rationale: Disabling the business rule that auto-denies Guest access removes a platform-wide safety net in one step, re-exposing every KB that relied on it.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11m-br-guest-use.best_practice: Keep the Guest User denial Business Rule active; treat any attempt to disable it as a high-priority security event.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11n-public-kb-pa.rationale: Marking KB view/find/home/list pages as public lets unauthenticated visitors reach knowledge content directly, bypassing portal and user-criteria controls.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11n-public-kb-pa.best_practice: Remove KB endpoint pages (kb_view, kb_find, kb_home, kb_list) from sys_public.list unless unauthenticated access is an explicit, reviewed requirement.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11o-public-kb-wi.rationale: Public KB widgets expose a server-side API that attackers can call unauthenticated, including enumerating/brute-forcing sequential KB numbers to harvest articles at scale.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11o-public-kb-wi.best_practice: Set public=false on KB-related Service Portal widgets; if public access is required, enforce user-criteria checks in the widget's server script, not just the portal page.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11p-acl-km-no-au.rationale: An unauthenticated Knowledge Management REST API gives attackers a direct, scriptable path to bulk-read KB content without ever touching the UI.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11p-acl-km-no-au.best_practice: Require authentication (and appropriate roles) on all sn_km_api endpoints; never leave the REST API ACL open to unauthenticated requests.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11q-acl-kb-empty.rationale: An empty ACL (no role, condition, or script) on the kb_knowledge table removes the table-level backstop, leaving protection entirely dependent on user criteria.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11q-acl-kb-empty.best_practice: Define a baseline role/condition on kb_knowledge ACLs so table-level access control doesn't rely solely on user criteria.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11r-acl-kb-custo.rationale: A custom ACL that's broader than intended can silently override or bypass the user-criteria model KB governance otherwise relies on.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11r-acl-kb-custo.best_practice: Review every custom ACL on kb_knowledge/kb_knowledge_base against the intended user-criteria model; remove or tighten any that grant broader access than criteria allow.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11s-kba-no-crite.rationale: Even within a generally restricted KB, individual published articles lacking their own criteria can be the weakest link an attacker finds first.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11s-kba-no-crite.best_practice: Audit published articles for missing criteria, especially in knowledge bases that are otherwise open or broadly accessible.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11t-kba-public-r.rationale: The public role on an article is a strong signal of intentional (or accidental) unauthenticated exposure and should be explicitly justified.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11t-kba-public-r.best_practice: Treat every article carrying the public role as a reviewed exception, not a default; remove it unless unauthenticated access is deliberate.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11u-uc-scripted-.rationale: Scripted user criteria can contain logic bugs or unintended always-true conditions that silently grant broader access than a declarative criteria would.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11u-uc-scripted-.best_practice: Code-review scripted user criteria for logic errors; prefer declarative (non-scripted) criteria unless scripting is strictly necessary.

level-knowledge/cstaces-11v-kb-commentin.rationale: Open commenting on KB articles can be abused to post phishing links or sensitive data, especially on externally-visible or sensitive-content knowledge bases.
level-knowledge/cstaces-11v-kb-commentin.best_practice: Disable commenting on sensitive or externally-facing KBs, or add moderation before comments become visible.

level-next/cstaces-10-sched-job-admin.rationale: A scheduled job running with admin privileges is a standing, unattended execution path — if its script or trigger conditions are tampered with, it runs attacker-controlled code with full admin rights on a timer.
level-next/cstaces-10-sched-job-admin.best_practice: Run scheduled jobs under the least-privileged role that completes the task; reserve admin-context jobs for platform-maintenance jobs only, with change control on their scripts.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

level-next/cstaces-5b-active-oauth.rationale: Active OAuth tokens/clients are durable, often long-lived credentials that let an attacker (or former integration) authenticate without a password or MFA prompt.
level-next/cstaces-5b-active-oauth.best_practice: Inventory and review all OAuth client/token grants quarterly; revoke unused tokens and set short, enforced expirations.

level-next/cstaces-6-br-priv-esc.rationale: Business Rules that run with elevated context (e.g., bypassing workflow/ACL enforcement while writing to security-relevant tables) can act as a built-in privilege-escalation or persistence mechanism baked into application logic.
level-next/cstaces-6-br-priv-esc.best_practice: Code-review Business Rules for patterns that grant roles, modify ACLs, or write to security tables; restrict who can create/edit Business Rules via scoped admin access and source control.

level-next/cstaces-7-ui-bypass.rationale: UI Policies that waive mandatory fields can let users (or an attacker driving the UI/API) submit incomplete or inconsistent records that evade downstream validation or approval logic.
level-next/cstaces-7-ui-bypass.best_practice: Audit UI Policies that make mandatory fields optional; ensure server-side validation (not just UI policy) enforces required data for security-relevant tables.

level-next/cstaces-9a-auth-session-prop.rationale: Weak session properties (long idle timeout, no concurrent-session limits) extend the usable window for a hijacked or shared session, giving an attacker more time to act under a valid session.
level-next/cstaces-9a-auth-session-prop.best_practice: Tighten session idle timeout and concurrent-session limits to the shortest values operationally acceptable; align with your SSO provider's session policy.

level-next/cstaces-9b-admin-no-mfa.rationale: Privileged accounts without MFA are single-factor-protected high-value targets — a leaked or guessed password alone is enough for full instance compromise.
level-next/cstaces-9b-admin-no-mfa.best_practice: Require MFA for all admin/security_admin accounts without exception, including break-glass accounts; enforce via MFA Policy or the identity provider.
